value.rationale: PASS: Matching both guild degree sequences and the entire expected-richness polynomial isolates structural dependence rather than degree artifacts. A sharp first possible nine-species reversal of variance order is a natural reliability boundary with an explicit single crossing, relevant to evaluating risk under changing extinction pressure. The result concerns a precise mathematical model and makes no unsupported field prediction.

final_claim: For one-stage independent equal-q pollinator extinction in bidegree-matched bipartite networks, no pair on <=8 total species reverses the surviving-plant richness variance order; a specific four-plant five-pollinator pair has variance difference -2q²(1-q)²(1-2q), reversing uniquely at q=1/2 with identical mean curves.
limitations: One-stage simple bipartite networks, homogeneous independent pollinator extinctions; no direct plant shocks, unequal edge weights, adaptive rewiring or cascading coextinctions.
Variance order is not stochastic ordering of full richness distributions.
Finite cutoff uses exact exhaustive enumeration; model-specific result not a general graph reliability classification.
